html:
SMTO-BOOT-0009 — Python couldn't create the Windows Gateway's program folder

GUID: e1c4f016-3640-4db4-abe1-6f8908616cd4
Slug: boot-environment-creation-failed
Domain: BOOT · Subsystem: boot

What happened

  • The Windows Gateway installer asked Python to create the Gateway's private program folder (.venv), and Python reported a failure. The Gateway wasn't installed or updated.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. In the PowerShell window, find the line that starts with Installation command failed and open the log file named after Details. The log shows Python's own reason, such as missing permission or a full disk.
  2. Make sure the drive holding the SMTO folder has free space and that your Windows account can create files in the src\gateway_windows folder. Python must write a full set of program files into that folder.
  3. Make sure the Python you're using is a complete 64-bit Python 3.11 or newer, such as the installer from python.org. Some cut-down Python packages can't create these program folders.
  4. Run src\gateway_windows\install.ps1 again. Once the cause is fixed, the installer creates the folder and continues setup.

What success looks like

  • The installer prints Windows gateway install complete.

If it still fails

  • Copy the PowerShell output and the log file it names, and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't delete other SMTO folders; the installer only rebuilds the Gateway's own .venv folder.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Windows Gateway installer ran the selected interpreter's venv module to create src\gateway_windows.venv and received a nonzero exit status.

What this means

  • The Windows installer invokes the selected interpreter's venv module and receives a nonzero exit status. Bootstrap diagnostics report the existing installer/launcher check only. They do not download packages, probe hardware, stop processes or change state while rendering; earlier setup steps may already have modified the environment.

Why this can happen

  • The Windows installer invokes the selected interpreter's venv module and receives a nonzero exit status.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the venv diagnostic, interpreter support and exact destination permissions/space.

How to fix it

  • Open the log path printed after 'Installation command failed' (or rerun install.ps1 with -Verbose), confirm the selected interpreter is a full 64-bit Python 3.11+ that includes the venv module, that the account can write src\gateway_windows, and that the volume has free space, then rerun the installer. The installer only removes an incompatible existing .venv before recreating it.
  • Inspect interpreter availability, destination permissions and available disk space, correct the reported prerequisite, then rerun the installer.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended environment is created successfully at its supported path.

What not to do

  • Do not remove retained state or weaken trust checks to make an unavailable dependency appear healthy.

Technical notes

  • Bootstrap diagnostics report the existing installer/launcher check only. They do not download packages, probe hardware, stop processes or change state while rendering; earlier setup steps may already have modified the environment.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
